title: Subordinate Clauses
subtitle: Master verb-final clauses and the 'Verb, Verb' bridge when a subordinate clause comes first.

cheatSheet.summary: Subordinating conjunctions (weil, dass, obwohl, wenn, ob, bevor, nachdem) open a subordinate clause (Nebensatz) and kick the conjugated verb all the way to the very end!
keyTakeaways: Standard Nebensatz: Main Clause + comma + Conjunction + Subject + ... + CONJUGATED VERB.
Fronted Nebensatz ('Verb, Verb' Rule): If the Nebensatz comes first, it occupies Position 1 of the entire sentence → the main clause verb MUST immediately follow the comma!
With modal/Perfekt verbs in a Nebensatz, the conjugated modal/auxiliary goes LAST (even after the infinitive/Partizip II!).
Coordinating conjunctions (ADUSO: aber, denn, und, sondern, oder) keep normal V2 order ('... denn ich bin müde').

patterns.example: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich müde bin.
patterns.translation: I'm staying home because I'm tired.

patterns.example: Wenn es regnet, nehme ich den Bus.
patterns.translation: When it rains, I take the bus.

patterns.example: Er sagt, dass er morgen kommen kann.
patterns.translation: He says that he can come tomorrow.

patterns.example: Ich lerne, denn ich habe eine Prüfung.
patterns.translation: I'm studying because I have an exam.

cheatSheet.watchOut: In a Perfekt Nebensatz, the auxiliary moves to the absolute end: '... weil ich das Buch gelesen HABE' (NOT 'habe gelesen').

exercises.instruction: Connect with 'weil' and send the conjugated verb to the very end.
exercises.english: I'm learning German because I live in Zurich.
exercises.fullGerman: Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich in Zürich wohne.
exercises.rulePill: 'weil' is a subordinating conjunction → it kicks the conjugated verb 'wohne' to the final slot of the clause.

exercises.instruction: Start with 'Wenn' and apply the 'Verb, Verb' bridge across the comma!
exercises.english: If I have time, I will visit you.
exercises.fullGerman: Wenn ich Zeit habe, besuche ich dich.
exercises.rulePill: The whole 'Wenn'-clause acts as Position 1 → the main verb 'besuche' must follow the comma immediately ('habe, besuche').

exercises.prompt: Wir gehen spazieren, ___ es draußen leicht regnet.
exercises.english: We go for a walk, although it is raining lightly outside.
exercises.fullGerman: Wir gehen spazieren, obwohl es draußen leicht regnet.
exercises.rulePill: 'obwohl' expresses contrast ('although') and sends 'regnet' to the end of the clause.

exercises.instruction: Place the modal verb LAST in the 'dass'-clause.
exercises.english: She hopes that she can travel to Japan soon.
exercises.fullGerman: Sie hofft, dass sie bald nach Japan reisen kann.
exercises.rulePill: Inside a subordinate clause, the conjugated modal ('kann') goes AFTER the infinitive ('reisen kann').

exercises.prompt: Ich weiß nicht genau, ___ der Zug pünktlich ankommt.
exercises.english: I don't know exactly whether the train arrives on time.
exercises.fullGerman: Ich weiß nicht genau, ob der Zug pünktlich ankommt.

nouns.caseTrigger: Subject of the indirect yes/no question

exercises.rulePill: Use 'ob' (never 'wenn') for 'whether / if' in indirect yes/no questions ('Ich weiß nicht, ob...').

exercises.promptHint: Notice the word order! One conjunction is wrong for V2 word order.
exercises.english: I'm coming later because I still have an appointment.
exercises.fullGerman: Ich komme später, denn ich habe noch einen Termin.
exercises.rulePill: Because 'habe' stays in Position 2, you MUST use coordinating 'denn' (Position 0), not subordinating 'weil'.

exercises.prompt: ___ ich ein Kind war, lebten wir auf dem Land.
exercises.english: When I was a child, we lived in the countryside.
exercises.fullGerman: Als ich ein Kind war, lebten wir auf dem Land.
exercises.rulePill: Use 'als' for a single past event or period ('When I was a child'), and 'wenn' for repeated/present/future events.

exercises.instruction: Put the Perfekt auxiliary at the very end of the 'obwohl'-clause.
exercises.english: He passed the exam even though he studied very little.
exercises.fullGerman: Er hat die Prüfung bestanden, obwohl er wenig gelernt hat.
exercises.rulePill: In a subordinate clause, the conjugated auxiliary 'hat' moves behind the Partizip II: '... wenig gelernt hat'.

exercises.promptHint: Inside a 'dass'-clause, separable verbs reunite AND conjugate for the subject!
exercises.english: I know that you get up early tomorrow.
exercises.fullGerman: Ich weiß, dass du morgen früh aufstehst.
exercises.rulePill: In a subordinate clause ('dass'), separable 'aufstehen' reunites at the end and conjugates for 'du': 'aufstehst'.
